bull_case: MELI has unusually broad reinvestment options across logistics, payments, credit and ads. High growth at scale suggests incremental capital still creates durable ecosystem value.
bear_case: The 2026 FCF slump shows reinvestment can consume cash rapidly. Credit and logistics may require ever-more capital while margins stay structurally lower.
thesis: Reinvestment quality remains strong enough for Compounder status, but this is the domain that deserves the closest monitoring. FY2025 adjusted FCF rose to $1.481B, yet H1 2026 fell to $158M as lending, restricted customer funds, capex and logistics absorbed cash. The runway is exceptional and share dilution is negligible, but full-cycle incremental ROIC must be judged on normalized credit losses and logistics economics rather than revenue growth alone.

evidence.claim: FY2025 adjusted FCF rose to $1.481B from $1.215B in 2024.
H1 2026 adjusted FCF fell to $158M from $512M despite 49% revenue growth.
H1 capex was $712M and loans receivable expanded materially as the credit portfolio grew.
Shares outstanding were essentially unchanged from year-end to Aug. 5, 2026.

counterevidence: Volume growth remains exceptional, supporting future operating leverage.
Credit, logistics and ads deepen ecosystem retention rather than being unrelated capex.
Low dilution preserves per-share participation in successful reinvestment.
unknowns: Risk-adjusted ROIC of Mercado Crédito by vintage.
Payback period on logistics and free-shipping investments.
Normalized adjusted FCF/share after growth intensity moderates.

uncertainties.rationale: Strong growth implies value creation, but current margin/FCF compression makes full-cycle returns uncertain.
Multiple large regional growth vectors remain.
Adjusted FCF is currently volatile because growth consumes cash.

falsifiers: Adjusted FCF/share stays depressed after growth investments mature.
Credit loss-adjusted returns fall below capital cost.
Logistics capex grows as fast as gross profit without retention or share benefits.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Current FCF compression reflects aggressive growth investment, while GMV/TPV/revenue growth does not show structural ROIC collapse.
Share count is essentially flat; current reinvestment is not being funded through material equity dilution.

key_kpis.name: Credit loss-adjusted return
key_kpis.threshold: Provision growth slows relative to financial income

key_kpis.name: Capex intensity
key_kpis.threshold: Capex grows slower than ecosystem gross profit over time

subscores.rationale: Historical scaling and ecosystem growth indicate strong returns, tempered by current margin pressure.
Commerce, fintech, credit, ads and logistics offer large long-duration reinvestment paths.
Low dilution is excellent, but current adjusted FCF is volatile and depressed.
